channel.title: The San Francisco Standard - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The San Francisco Standard (sfstandard.com)

item.title: Is the Shvo over at the Transamerica Pyramid?
item.description: The developer’s German investors are experiencing buyer’s remorse after pouring retirement savings into remaking the San Francisco icon.

item.title: Guns, meth, slot machines: Contraband in Tenderloin stores spurs call for expanded curfew
item.description: Supervisors will vote in February on extending a late-night curfew for stores on crime-ridden streets.

item.title: The 5 most exciting SF restaurants opening in February
item.description: The couple behind Dalida will debut a Mexican restaurant called Maria Isabel in Pacific Heights, while Polk Street welcomes a retro-style diner.

item.title: San Jose mayor Matt Mahan enters gridlocked race for California governor
item.description: He has been a frequent critic of Gov. Gavin Newsom. Now he wants his job.

item.title: Waymo begins operating at SFO, just in time for Super Bowl
item.description: Pickups and drop offs will take place for now at the SFO Rental Car Center and eventually expand to the terminals.

item.title: Reid Hoffman: Silicon Valley can’t be neutral any longer
item.description: After Minneapolis, tech leaders’ deference to Donald Trump must end.

item.title: Ikea’s food hall starts new chapter amid closed bars and restaurants
item.description: Saluhall eagerly welcomed a new restaurant Thursday, but vacancies abound.

item.title: ‘What happened in Minnesota can happen here’: Bay Area readies for Friday strike
item.description: Restaurant owners, climbing gyms, and boutiques are sacrificing their busiest sales day to join a strike sparked by fatal shootings in Minneapolis.

item.title: Lurie leans on task force to clean up baffling city charter
item.description: Labor unions have opposed limiting the ability to put measures on the ballot, citing the need to even the playing field with business interests.

item.title: Messy SF homeless count hampered by new rules
item.description: For the first time, homeless counters were required to speak to everyone they tallied. It made for a slower, weirder morning — and possibly a lower count.
